### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Cadherins are the molecules that join epithelial cells to each other by forming adherens junctions. Integrins, although important in connecting the extracellular matrix to the cell cytoskeleton, are not directly involved in joining epithelial cells to each other. Fibronectins bind to integrins and aid in cell adhesion and migration but are not directly involved in connecting epithelial cells. Elastins provide tissue elasticity and are not involved in joining epithelial cells. Laminins, as major components of basement membranes, indirectly contribute to the connection between epithelial cells by providing structural support.
